JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 19.7.2022 at about 6.15 p.m. the petitioner was returning from his work place Budigere-Nalluru road on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-40-EB-7807 (Bajaj CT 100) slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Nagenahalli, at that time, driver of the Truk bearing registration No.KA-01-AD-6543 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Shiradi Sai Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and had spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.

4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 44 years, working in a Gas Company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
Venkatesh.

sentences.text: It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Truck bearing No.KA-01-AD-6543.

In this regard,
case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Chennarayapatna Police Station, Devanahalli in Crime No.64/2022 under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company, the respondent No.2 being the owner and the respondent No.3 being the driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.1, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Truck bearing No.KA-01-AD-6543 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that the driver of the Truck had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of the accident.

It is also contention of the respondent that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-40-EB-7807 (Bajaj CT 100) and not on the part of the driver of the Truck.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
8. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has stated that the respondent No.1 has issued policy in respect of Truck bearing No.KA-01- AD-6543 and the said policy at the time of accident.
Further stated that the driver of the Truck had valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also manner of the accident as claimed in the petition.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

9. The respondent No.3 has stated that, he is the driver of the Truck and he had valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the vehicle had valid policy, hence respondent No.1 is the indemnifier by virtue of contract of insurance as per law.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on his part.
Hence, he prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

10. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 19.7.2022 at about 6.15 p.m. Nalluru cross-Budigere road, Nagenahalli Venkatesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124593979/
3 village main road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Truck bearing registration No.KA-01-AD- 6543, in an actionable negligence?

12.

14.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

15.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Truck bearing registration No.KA-01- AD-6543, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently
he had sustained grievous injuries.
16. On the other hand, the respondents, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the manner of accident.
But not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.
In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the court to assess the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion in connection with the above fact in issue.
17. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
PW1 in his examination- in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P16.
Ex. P1
-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.64/2022 of Channarayapatna Police Station.

18. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Channarayapatna Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

19. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
20. Moreover, the respondents have filed the written statement, but not led any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the contention of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.

21. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Truck bearing registration No.KA- 01-AD-6543.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
22.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

23. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as Venkatesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124593979/

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P3.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Laceration of left knee 2) Injury over left hip and deformity 3) injury over left wrist and swelling CT fact-multiple facial bone fracture CT pelvic -displaced fracture of posterior of superior wall of left acetabulam x-ray left wrist-comminuted fracture of left distal radious X-ray shows left knee-comminuted fracture of left patella 25.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary, lab report, medical bills as per Ex.P17 to Ex.P19.

On going through the discharge summary of Shirdi Sai Hopital,
Bengaluru reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 19.7.2022 to 29.7.2022.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Manjunatha Reddy C. as PW2.

PW2 has placed clinical note &
x-ray as per Ex.P23 to Ex.P28.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
26.

PW1 has stated that, he was working in Gas Company at Chemix Speciality Gases & Equipment and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/-
per month.

In this regard, he has placed salary certificate issued by Chemix Speciality Gases &
Equipment, Bengaluru as per Ex.P22, which reveals that the petitioner was getting salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
To prove the same, the petitioner has not examined his employer or his pass book to show the definite income.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken.
On going through the discharge summary of Shiradi Sai Hospital, Bengaluru reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 19.7.2022 to 29.7.2022.

During the period of treatment, definitely,
there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least Venkatesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124593979/
6 for a period of three months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.

sentences.text: Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.46,500/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
27.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.11,56.721/- as per Ex.P19.
At the time of cross-examination respondent No.1 has suggested that Sl.No.2,3,8 to 16 are the advance bills the said bills are included in the Sl.No.28.
For which PW1 has admitted the same.
On calculation of the entire medical bills the total amount comes to Rs.4,80,243/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs..4,80,243/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
28.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
29.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P3 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment for a period of 10 days.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summary for consideration.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Manjunatha Reddy C. examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained left side zygomatic bone fracture, left wrist distal radius comminuted intra articular fracture, left hip posterior fracture dislocation, left patella comminuted fracture.

For which the petitioner underwent ORIF with plate fixation for zygomatic fracture, ORIF with plate and screws for left distal radius fracture, ORIF with posterior acetabular wall plating for left hip ORIF with TBW for patella and later he was discharged with regular follow-up treatment.

He has placed clinical assessment report, x-rays, old x-rays, CT scan, entire case sheet along with authorisation letter as per Ex.P23 to Ex.P28.
30.
PW2 has stated that, at the time of his examination the petitioner has gait--walker assisted severe antalgic gait, left hip, attitude, adduction and internal rotation, tenderness on left knee.
X-ray shows left hip femoral head deformed with arthritic and avascular changes, left wrist fracture united with implant insitu, left patella fracture united with implant in situ.

sentences.text: At the time of cross-examination of PW2, denied the suggestion that due to the accidental injuries the petitioner has not sustained any disability.
Based on the documents he has assessed the physical disability.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.

32. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as left lower limb is 78% and whole body both upper and lower limb is 25% seems little bit exorbitant.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 17% instead of 25%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
33. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 44 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P20 for consideration.
On going through the said documents, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 11.8.1978.
The accident occurred on 19.7.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 44 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '14' is to be taken into consideration.

34. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, he was working at Gas Company and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
As already discussed above, though the petitioner has placed salary certificate, but not examined his employer, acquaintance book or bank pass book to prove the said income.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.

35. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X 12 X 14 X17/100= Rs.4,42,680/-.
Loss of amenities;
36.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he is unable to eat food, very difficult to move about and undergoing deep mental shock and agony.

On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.

The estimate of this surgery is around Rs.1,00,000/-
and removal of implants from the left wrist and knee the approximate cost of the same is around Rs.60,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses.

38. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 60,000-00  2.Loss of income during Rs. 46,500-00  laid-up period and rest  period  3.
Medical expenses Rs. 4,80,243-00  4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 20,000-00  and Conveyance Charges  5. Loss of future income Rs. 4,42,680-00  due to disability  6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 30,000-00  7.
Future medication Rs. 50,000-00  Total Rs.11,29,423-00 39.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,29,423/- (Rupees eleven lakh twenty nine thousand four hundred and twenty three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
40.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Truck bearing registration No.KA-01-AD-6543,
alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 & 3 being the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
41. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 23.2.2022 to 22.2.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 19.7.2022.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being owner of the of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.3 being the driver is not necessary party when the owner is on record as he is acted according to his master's advice.

9 view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.

ISSUE NO.3:
42.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,29,423/- (Rupees eleven lakh twenty nine thousand four hundred and twenty three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,29,423/- (Rupees eleven lakh twenty nine thousand four hundred and twenty three only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
